name: org.machanism.machai:mcp-server-maven-plugin
description: MCP Server Maven Plugin is a Java 17 Maven plugin that launches a Machai Model Context Protocol (MCP) server as part of a Maven build. It exposes configured Machai AI tools over HTTP without a separate server launcher, supporting local development, integration testing, demonstrations, and build-driven AI workflows. The plugin provides the aggregator goals stateless and streamable, which respectively start stateless HTTP and streamable HTTP MCP server transports using the current Maven project name, version, and base directory. Both goals apply configured parameters as JVM system properties without replacing properties already supplied to the process, load the MCP configuration file, configure the listener port, and report startup failures as Maven execution errors. The plugin supports reactor builds where one server should represent the complete multi-module build. It also exposes the MCP function tool stop_mcp_server, supported for McpServer, for an orderly delayed JVM shutdown after a client completes its work. Configure mcp.port, mcp.config, and optional params values in Maven or on the command line; use Maven settings credentials when the server configuration requires them.

constructors.description: Creates the function-tools component that exposes the MCP server lifecycle shutdown operation to a running Machai MCP server.

examples.description: For an embedded Java integration, create the lifecycle tool and request a normal shutdown. In ordinary plugin use, the MCP server registers this tool from its configuration rather than application code creating it directly.

features.name: stateless
features.description: Starts a stateless HTTP MCP server as an aggregator Maven goal. It applies parameters and credentials, initializes the server from Maven project metadata and the configured MCP file, sets the project directory and HTTP port, then starts the endpoint. This is suitable when a stateless MCP HTTP transport is required.

examples.description: Step 1: add the plugin configuration to the consuming Maven project's build, which installs the ready-to-use Maven component through normal dependency resolution. Step 2: create an MCP properties file at the configured path with the Machai server and tool settings. Step 3: invoke the stateless goal with the required port and configuration location. Connect an MCP-compatible HTTP client while Maven remains running.

features.name: streamable
features.description: Starts a streamable HTTP MCP server as an aggregator Maven goal. It uses the same project metadata, configuration, parameters, credentials, base directory, and port handling as the stateless goal, but selects the streamable HTTP transport for clients and deployments that require it.

examples.description: Step 1: resolve the plugin by invoking its fully specified Maven coordinates. Step 2: supply a readable Machai MCP configuration through mcp.config and choose an available HTTP port through mcp.port. Step 3: run the streamable goal and configure the real MCP client to use the resulting streamable HTTP endpoint.

features.name: stopMcpServer
features.description: Initiates an orderly delayed MCP server shutdown, logs the shutdown event, and exits the JVM with the supplied exit code. The default MCP function argument is 0, indicating normal completion. This function tool is supported for McpServer.

examples.description: After an MCP client has completed a local development or test workflow, invoke the registered stop_mcp_server function with exit_code 0. The server returns an acknowledgement, waits briefly for the response to complete, records shutdown activity, and terminates normally.

customizations.name: mcp.config
customizations.description: Maven property identifying the readable MCP server configuration file used to load server and tool settings. It should be supplied for server startup.

examples.description: Pass the configuration file path at invocation time to keep environment-specific configuration outside the project POM.

customizations.name: params
customizations.description: Optional map of environment-style values copied to JVM system properties only when the property has not already been provided. A server identifier can resolve credentials from Maven settings.

examples.title: Run a local stateless MCP endpoint
steps: Add org.machanism.machai:mcp-server-maven-plugin:1.3.0 to the Maven build or invoke it directly by coordinates.
Prepare an mcp.properties file containing Machai MCP server and tool configuration.
Connect an MCP-compatible HTTP client to the configured endpoint and use its registered tools.
When the workflow is complete, invoke stop_mcp_server with exit_code 0 for orderly shutdown.
